findings.title: Human-in-loop broken
findings.body:
The old `askHuman` tool had no `execute`, so the model stopped and waited for a human to answer. The new `createTool` adds a `handler` that returns the question right away. The SDK will now run the tool and send the question back to the model as its own answer. The human is never asked.

This also breaks `humanResponseAsToolCall`, which later saves a second `tool-result` for the same `toolCallId`. Remove the handler, or define the tool without an execute function, to keep the old flow.

findings.title: Invalid tool-result
findings.body:
In AI SDK v5, a `tool-result` part's `output` must be a typed object such as `{ type: "text", value: ... }` or `{ type: "json", value: ... }`. Here a raw string is assigned and cast `as any`, which hides the mismatch.

The cast makes the code compile, but the saved message will have an invalid shape. It may fail validation or be rejected when the message is turned back into a prompt for the model.

findings.title: Wrong model type
findings.body:
`chat` is now typed as `LanguageModelV1`, which goes backwards from the previous `LanguageModelV2`. With v5 providers, the models are `LanguageModelV2`.

- The OpenAI branch forces the assignment with `as any`.
- The Groq branch has no cast, so it will likely not type-check.
- Every agent now uses `chat as any`, which hides real type errors.

Also, `openai.languageModel(...)` replaces `openai.chat(...)`. In v5 this may use the Responses API instead of Chat Completions, which changes runtime behavior. Keep the `LanguageModelV2` type and drop the casts.
